title: How does image generation work?
reading: The slide introduces diffusion-based image generation by contrasting two directions: a forward diffusion process that progressively corrupts an image, and a reverse denoising/generation process that reconstructs an image from noise. Ellipses indicate intermediate steps in each chain, implying many small incremental steps rather than a single transformation. The summary line states the core idea of diffusion models: Gaussian noise is gradually added, and a model is trained to reverse that corruption, which is what allows sampling new images from noise.

visuals.description: A two-directional chain of intermediate image states, labelled 'Diffusion process' in one direction and 'Denoising/generation process' in the other, with ellipses marking omitted intermediate steps.
visuals.assertion: Image generation is the learned reverse of a stepwise noising process running between a clean image and pure noise.
